newsitem.title: UK: EBRD plans 30mln Ecu Bulgaria venture capital fund.
newsitem.headline: EBRD plans 30mln Ecu Bulgaria venture capital fund.

text.p: The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) said it was looking for a fund management firm to manage a planned 30 million Ecu ($31.8 million) Bulgaria venture capital fund.
The bank said in an official tender dated July 30 that the fund would be established in Bulgaria in late 1997 or early 1998, subject to the final decision of the bank and the European Union.

The fund will be a closed-end 10-year equity fund. It will target investments in medium-sized, domestically owned Bulgarian private and privatised companies with the purpose of rationalising, modernising or expanding their production facilities.

It said the fund manager would be expected to invest the fund's capital within approximately three to four years as direct equity investments in companies with good growth prospects and a core focus on domestic markets.
The anticipated minimum investment will be 300,000 Ecu, with a maximum of three million ECU in each target enterprise.
It would be expected to exit from the investments within 10 years and earn a commercial rate of return on the portfolio in line with project risks.
The EBRD said expressions of interest in the management contract should be received no later than September 5.
-- Andrew Gill, London newsroom +171 542 5887 ($ = 0.943 European Currency Unit ECUs)
